summary_headline: Endpoint protection is strong, but recovery and remote access are unproven
summary: Globex’s 58 managed endpoints all run SentinelOne in full Protect mode, with no infected devices and no internet-exposed RDP or file-sharing ports. The risk sits elsewhere: only one of twelve servers shows a visible backup agent, remote-access software from several different providers reaches servers, the SSL-VPN is absorbing roughly ten failed logins for every real connection, and identity and domain-controller logging are largely dark, so an intrusion would be hard to see and harder to reconstruct.
board_ask: direct management to confirm, within 14 days, that every server has an immutable, recently tested backup, and to remove or approve every remote-access tool on servers. Sponsor a 90-day program to enforce VPN MFA and restore identity and server logging so readiness can be measured.

pillars.detail: Backup agent visible on 1 of 12 servers

pillars.name: Remote Access
pillars.detail: 6 ScreenConnect instances plus AnyDesk, TeamViewer, LogMeIn; VPN under password attack

pillars.name: Logging & Forensics

pillars.name: Identity & Access

pillars.name: Vulnerability Exposure
pillars.detail: 16 endpoints need patches; no CVE scanner feed

pillars.name: Endpoint Coverage
pillars.detail: 58 agents active, all seen within 16 days

issues.title: Backup protection cannot be verified for 11 of 12 servers
issues.finding: Across the application inventory of all 12 servers, only one shows a backup agent (Datto Windows Agent). No enterprise backup product is visible on the other 11. Backups may be taken at the hypervisor level, but nothing in the telemetry confirms coverage, immutability or restore testing.
issues.why: Recoverable backups are what lets an organization refuse a ransom. If backups are missing, reachable from the network, or untested, a single attack can halt operations for weeks.
issues.recommendation: Within 14 days, produce a server-by-server backup inventory, confirm at least one immutable or offline copy, keep backup consoles off the production domain, and run a timed full-restore test of a critical server. Add backup-job health to monthly reporting.

issues.title: Uncontrolled remote-access software reaches servers
issues.finding: ScreenConnect clients connect to six different ScreenConnect instances, not one: a second instance is installed on 3 servers, and one server runs a 2021-era client for yet another instance. AnyDesk (a 2020 release), TeamViewer and LogMeIn are also installed on servers. A user-downloaded ScreenConnect installer was flagged by EDR in the last 180 days.
issues.why: Each unknown remote-access instance is a standing door into the network controlled by someone outside IT. Ransomware groups routinely use exactly these tools, or a vendor’s compromised account, to enter and deploy encryption.
issues.recommendation: Identify the owner of every ScreenConnect instance; uninstall any that are not approved. Standardize on one remote-access platform with MFA and session logging, remove AnyDesk, TeamViewer and LogMeIn from servers, and block unapproved remote-access tools by EDR policy.

issues.title: The SSL-VPN is under sustained password-guessing pressure
issues.finding: In 30 days the FortiGate logged 951 failed SSL-VPN logins against 98 successful new connections, roughly ten failures for every genuine session. SSL-VPN is exposed on its standard port.
issues.why: Compromised or brute-forced VPN accounts are one of the most common ways ransomware groups get in. Without MFA, one weak password is enough.
issues.recommendation: Confirm MFA (Duo) is enforced on every VPN login, apply account lockout and geo-restrictions, keep FortiOS on the latest patched release, and plan migration from SSL-VPN to IPsec or zero-trust access.

issues.title: Domain and server activity is largely unlogged
issues.finding: Windows Security audit events arrive from only 9 of 58 hosts (one domain controller), and the datalake holds less than a day of history. There is no 30-day record of log clearing, new admin accounts, service installs or lateral movement.
issues.why: If an attack happens, investigators, insurers and regulators will ask what the attacker did and for how long. Without these logs that question cannot be answered, and early warning signs go unseen.
issues.recommendation: Forward Security, System and PowerShell logs from all domain controllers and servers, retain them for at least 90 days, and alert on log clearing, new privileged accounts and new services.

issues.title: Identity sign-in monitoring is dark
issues.finding: No Entra ID sign-in records have reached the datalake, and MFA registration data is not collected, so administrator MFA cannot be verified. Microsoft 365 audit data shows 540 failed logins against 317 successful ones across 10 accounts in 30 days. 3 accounts hold Global Administrator.
issues.why: Stolen credentials are the leading ransomware entry point. Without sign-in visibility, a compromised administrator account could be used without anyone noticing.
issues.recommendation: Repair the Entra sign-in connector and grant authentication-method reporting. Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all administrators through Conditional Access, and review the failing accounts.

issues.title: EDR alert noise is hiding the signal
issues.finding: SentinelOne raised 397 detections in 180 days; about 95% are copies of remote-support binaries saved by Dell SupportAssist’s remediation feature. 366 are still marked “suspicious” with no analyst conclusion, and 3 remain unresolved.
issues.why: When most alerts are noise, the one that matters (a scanner, a credential dumper, an encryption test run) is easily dismissed or missed.
issues.recommendation: Add a targeted exclusion for the Dell SupportAssist remediation folder, close the backlog, and set a triage time target for every new detection.

issues.title: Patch status and vulnerabilities are only partly visible
issues.finding: 16 of 58 endpoints report applications needing patches, including 6 of 12 servers. One Windows 10 device is past end of support and one Server 2016 host reaches end of support in January 2027. No vulnerability scanner feeds the SIEM, so exploitable CVEs cannot be measured.
issues.why: Known, weaponized vulnerabilities are a leading ransomware entry point, and the organization currently cannot see which ones it has.
issues.recommendation: Patch the 6 servers first, replace the end-of-life systems, and connect a vulnerability scanner (for example SentinelOne Ranger/Singularity Vulnerability Management or Defender VM) to the SIEM.

issues.title: Reconnaissance and file-transfer tools on servers
issues.finding: A network scanner (Advanced IP Scanner) is installed on a server, alongside file-transfer tools including a 2013-era WinSCP release, FileZilla and PuTTY.
issues.why: Attackers favor tools already present on the network: scanners to map targets and transfer tools to steal data before encrypting it.
issues.recommendation: Remove tools without a documented business need, restrict the remainder to named admin accounts, and alert when they run.

roadmap.actions: Server backup inventory with immutable copy and restore test; identify and remove unapproved ScreenConnect instances and remote-access tools on servers; confirm Duo MFA on every VPN login.
roadmap.outcome: Recovery proven; outside access doors closed.

roadmap.actions: Repair Entra sign-in feed; admin MFA via Conditional Access; forward DC and server logs with 90-day retention; tune Dell SupportAssist noise and clear the alert backlog.
Patch servers; connect a vulnerability scanner; remove scanning and transfer tools; VPN lockout and geo-restriction.
Replace end-of-life systems; plan SSL-VPN to IPsec or zero-trust migration; ransomware tabletop exercise with the executive team.

strengths: All 58 SentinelOne agents run in Protect mode for both malicious and suspicious threats.
No infected endpoints and no active threats at the time of assessment.
No RDP, SMB or SSH exposed inbound from the internet in a 7-day firewall review.
Every agent has checked in within 16 days and all but one run a current version.
methodology: Findings were derived from Globex’s Fluency / Ingext datalake: SentinelOne agent, threat (180 days) and application inventories; FortiGate traffic (7 days) and VPN events (30 days); Microsoft 365 audit events and Entra user snapshots (30 days); and Windows Security audit events. Microsoft Defender and Entra sign-in data are not present for this tenant, so OS hardening, CVE exposure and administrator MFA could not be measured and are reported as visibility gaps. Server backup coverage is inferred from installed software; hypervisor-level backups would not appear. No individual users are named in this report. Sanitized sample — company and identity details are fictional.
